# AWS API Gateway

This plugin collects read-only metadata for AWS API Gateway custom domain names, evaluates CCF Rego policy bundles against each domain, and emits evidence back through the CCF agent.

This page is for **operators** who run the `plugin-aws-apigateway` plugin with the CCF Agent, and for **developers** who write policies for it. It documents [v0.1.2](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-aws-apigateway/releases/tag/v0.1.2) and is generated from the plugin's [README at v0.1.2](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-aws-apigateway/blob/v0.1.2/README.md).

## How it works

### How it fits in CCF

The CCF agent starts this binary through HashiCorp `go-plugin` (runner protocol v2), passes configuration and policy paths over gRPC, and receives generated evidence through the runner callback. This repository does not call the CCF API directly.

During `Init`, the plugin registers the `apigateway-domain` subject template (identified by `account_id`, `region` and `domain_name`) and the subject and risk templates discovered from the supplied policy bundles.

## Configuration

| Key | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `regions` | yes | Comma-separated list of AWS regions to scan. Empty entries are ignored. |
| `policy_labels` | no | JSON object of extra labels added to every evidence, e.g. `{"team":"platform"}`. |

AWS credentials come from the default AWS SDK credential chain. The account ID is read with `sts:GetCallerIdentity` in the first configured region.

Any agent-supplied `policy_data` is passed through to Rego as `data.*`, on top of the bundle's own `data.json` (agent-supplied keys win).

## Evidence collected

### Data collected

For every custom domain name returned by the API Gateway `GetDomainNames` API (all pages) in each configured region, the plugin builds this policy input:

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `region` | the region scanned |
| `account_id` | the caller's AWS account |
| `domain_name` | the custom domain name |
| `security_policy` | the domain's TLS security policy |
| `certificate_arn` | the regional certificate ARN, or the edge-optimized one when there is no regional certificate (omitted when neither is set) |
| `endpoint_type` | the first endpoint type (e.g. `REGIONAL`, `EDGE`) |
| `status` | the domain name status |
| `tags` | the domain's tags |

Each evidence carries the labels `provider=aws`, `type=apigateway-domain`, `domain_name`, `region` and `account_id`, plus any `policy_labels`.

## Policy input

One document per API Gateway custom domain name, in each configured region. The plugin builds it from `GetDomainNames`, and a policy reads it as `input`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `region` | string | AWS region the domain is defined in. |
| `account_id` | string | AWS account ID the plugin is running against. |
| `domain_name` | string | The custom domain name. |
| `security_policy` | string | The domain's TLS security policy, for example `TLS_1_2` or `TLS_1_0`. |
| `certificate_arn` | string | ARN of the certificate on the domain: the regional certificate when there is one, otherwise the edge-optimized one. Omitted when the domain has none. |
| `endpoint_type` | string | First endpoint type of the domain: `EDGE`, `REGIONAL` or `PRIVATE`. Empty when none is set. |
| `status` | string | Domain name status, for example `AVAILABLE`, `UPDATING` or `PENDING`. |
| `tags` | object (string to string) | The domain's tags. An empty object when it has none. |

An example input:

```json
{
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "account_id": "111122223333",
  "domain_name": "api.example.com",
  "security_policy": "TLS_1_2",
  "certificate_arn": "arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:111122223333:certificate/3f1c2d4e-5a6b-4c7d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f",
  "endpoint_type": "REGIONAL",
  "status": "AVAILABLE",
  "tags": {
    "Environment": "production"
  }
}
```

## Subject templates

The subject templates this plugin registers. Each example is built from sample data.

### apigateway-domain

An API Gateway custom domain. The plugin registers it as a component subject and attaches it to the evidence of every domain it evaluates. Title: `API Gateway Domain {{ .domain_name }}`.

| Identity key | Description |
|---|---|
| `account_id` | AWS account ID. |
| `region` | AWS region. |
| `domain_name` | API Gateway custom domain name. |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "apigateway-domain",
  "type": "component",
  "title": "API Gateway Domain api.example.com",
  "description": "AWS API Gateway custom domain api.example.com in 111122223333/eu-west-1.",
  "purpose": "Represents an AWS API Gateway custom domain evaluated for TLS compliance posture.",
  "identityLabels": {
    "account_id": "111122223333",
    "region": "eu-west-1",
    "domain_name": "api.example.com"
  }
}
```
